messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight 'surface splitter' pattern for hosted/dedicated/private. split into Capability Descriptor (what) and Runtime Contract (how). keeps semantics explicit and enables probe-first validation.
aj: short sketch pls — auth and cache always get funky.
maria: descriptor example below (very small):
```
capability.identity = [token, mtls]
capability.kv_cache = none | shared | prefetch
capability.quota.scope = token | route | tenant
capability.network_requirements = none | intra-vpc
capability.descriptor_version = v1

runtime.latency_slo_ms = 150
runtime.max_tokens = 4096
runtime.error_categories = [TRANSIENT, PERMANENT, AUTHZ, QUOTA]
runtime.rollout = optional {canary_percent, monitoring_hooks}
```
sahil: two blindspots: auth translation (hosted injects platform identity; private won't)  we need a canonical handshake translation. and quotas: dedicated wants commit semantics while hosted meters. descriptor.quota.enforcement controlplane|runtime solves that.
kevin: if kv_cache==shared require network_requirements=intra-vpc; private should default to none. also surface observability.min fields for token_latency, kv_hit_rate, fallback_count.
lucy: standardize error categories in runtime so apps map consistently to HTTP. add compatibility version so older control planes can reject unknown descriptors.
ops-bot: created CI job template hosting-surface-smoke (auth handshake, kv warmup, fallback exercise): https://ci/internal/job/hosting-surface-smoke
maria: next steps: i'll draft an addendum with descriptor schema, handshake sequence diagram, and a small test matrix. sahil will own the test matrix. please flag gaps now. :thumbsup:
